transfers.source_mechanism: Hierarchical surface structures with directional features reduce resistance to directional flow while inhibiting attachment.
transfers.target_problem: A municipal water pipeline (10 km, 0.5 m diameter, Re=500,000) uses smooth HDPE pipe with friction factor f=0.013. Chemical drag reducers are prohibited. A passive surface treatment is needed that reduces pressure drop by at least 5%, is food-grade, survives 20 years, and can be retrofitted to existing pipes.
transfers.transferred_principle: Directional microstructures on the pipe inner surface modify boundary layer dynamics to reduce drag and inhibit particle/biofilm attachment.
transfers.required_translation: Replace fish skin scales with precisely engineered polymer microstructures (aligned ridges or grooves) on food-grade HDPE lining. Material must be NSF/61 certified polymer with elastic modulus matching HDPE. Surface features must be 50-200 micrometers high, aligned with flow direction, and arranged in a hierarchical pattern.
transfers.expected_effect: Reduced friction factor by at least 5% (f≤0.01235) while maintaining cleanability through pigging operations.
transfers.testable_prediction: Pipes with transferred microstructure treatment will show a measurable reduction in pressure drop (≥5%) compared to smooth HDPE controls in a 1-year operational test with periodic pigging, with no measurable increase in biofilm thickness in the treated sections.
